item.prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

Use a ____ marker for the sign so the rain will not wash the words away.
choices: permenent
permanant
permanent
permenant
item.spelling_pattern: two unstressed vowels: the middle a and the -ent ending
error_sites: unstressed a in the second syllable

student_error.permenent: writes e for the unstressed a sound in the middle syllable
student_error.permenant: writes e for the middle a and also ends the word in -ant

item.explanation: "permanent" is the correct spelling (unstressed a in the second syllable; -ent ending). "permenent" writes e for the unstressed a sound in the middle syllable. "permanant" uses -ant instead of -ent. "permenant" writes e for the middle a and also ends the word in -ant.

item.prompt: Which sentence has a spelling error?
choices: Leo faced a dilemna when both of his friends invited him to parties on the same night.
My mother's colleague brought cookies to the office on Friday.
A young entrepreneur opened a bakery on our street.
The camaraderie among the team members grew stronger with every game they played together this season.
item.correct_answer: Leo faced a dilemna when both of his friends invited him to parties on the same night.

student_error.My mother's colleague brought cookies to: colleague has a double l and ends in -ague, so it looks unusual
student_error.A young entrepreneur opened a bakery on: entrepreneur ends in -eur, which a student may think should be -er or -ure
student_error.The camaraderie among the team members g: camaraderie has an a where many students expect an e or nothing (comradery)

item.explanation: The key misspells "dilemma" as "dilemna" (mm written as mn). The other sentences are spelled correctly: "colleague", "entrepreneur", "camaraderie".

item.correct_answer: Every summer our town holds a parade on Independence Day, and every fall it holds a pumpkin fair behind the library.

student_error.Every Summer our town holds a parade on: Capitalizes 'summer' because it names a time of year, like the holiday in the same sentence.
student_error.Every summer our town holds a parade on: Capitalizes 'fall' because it names a time of year, the way months and holidays are capitalized.
student_error.Every Summer our town holds a parade on: Believes seasons are capitalized like months and holidays.

item.explanation: Independence Day is the name of a holiday and is capitalized, but seasons such as summer and fall are common nouns and stay lowercase. 'pumpkin fair' is not the name of an event here.
item.cap_rule: seasons stay lowercase while a holiday is capitalized

item.cap_rule: nationality adjectives and names of languages

choices: We took a long windy walk past the three old, red barns on Miller Road.

item.correct_answer: We took a long, windy walk past the three old red barns on Miller Road.
error_sites: comma between the coordinate adjectives 'long' and 'windy'
comma between the cumulative adjectives 'old' and 'red'

student_error.We took a long windy walk past the three: Leaves out the comma between two adjectives that each describe the walk equally.
student_error.We took a long, windy walk past the thre: Puts a comma between 'old' and 'red', though they cannot be joined by 'and' or switched.

item.explanation: 'long, windy walk' needs a comma because 'long and windy' makes sense and the order can switch. 'old red barns' takes no comma because 'old and red barns' or 'red old barns' sounds wrong: the adjectives are cumulative.
item.punct_rule: comma between coordinate adjectives but not cumulative ones

student_error.This morning they told us our books are: Uses 'they' the way people talk, without naming who told them.
student_error.This morning the librarian told us our b: Uses 'it says' with no noun for 'it' to refer to.

item.explanation: A pronoun needs a clear antecedent. 'they' and 'it' refer to no noun in the sentence, so the clear version names the librarian and has the newsletter itself as the subject.
